n: The heading connects this psalm to “Cush the Benjamite,” possibly a follower of Saul who slandered David. David takes refuge in God and asks to be saved from his pursuers.

f.w: in thee do I put my trust

n: Otherwise his enemy will tear him apart like a lion, with no one to rescue him.
David invites God to examine him: if he has done what he is accused of, if his hands are guilty…

f.g: A formal oath of innocence, like Job’s.

n: …if he has betrayed a friend — when in fact he spared the one who was his enemy without cause…

f.w: I have delivered him that without cause is mine enemy
f.g: Perhaps recalling how David spared Saul’s life.

n: …then let his enemy hunt him down, trample his life into the ground, and lay his honor in the dust.

f.w: lay mine honour in the dust
f.g: Honor (literally “glory”) here can also mean his very life.

n: David calls on God to rise up in anger against his raging enemies and wake to carry out the justice he has decreed.

f.g: Bold poetic language — not that God sleeps, but a plea for him to act.

n: Let the nations gather around God’s throne as he takes his seat on high to judge.
The Lord judges the peoples. David asks to be judged by his integrity — not claiming sinlessness, but innocence of these charges.
End the evil of the wicked and secure the righteous, for God tests minds and hearts.

f.g: Reins = kidneys, thought of as the seat of emotions — God examines our deepest motives.

n: David’s shield is God, who saves the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge and opposes evil every day.

f.w: God is angry with the wicked every day
f.g: Better “a God who expresses his displeasure every day” — his justice never sleeps.

n: If people don’t repent, God sharpens his sword and strings his bow.
He prepares deadly weapons and makes his arrows flaming darts.

f.w: ordaineth his arrows against the persecutors

n: The wicked are pictured as pregnant with evil: they conceive trouble and give birth to lies.
Whoever digs a pit to trap others falls into it himself.

f.w: is fallen into the ditch which he made

n: The trouble he causes comes back on his own head; his violence lands on his own skull.

f.w: His mischief shall return upon his own head

n: David ends in praise, thanking the Lord for his justice and singing to the Most High.

f.g: Hebrew ‘Elyon, an ancient title for God.
